## Mission
Quick demo prototype of a gear-depot checkout planner for an upcoming pitch. Speed and feature breadth over reliability.

## Still Owed
**L5 — Performance benchmark suite (not yet run).** Before any further features: timing report on plan generation and application with large fixtures (hundreds of items, thousands of requests). Numbers must be written down. Ordinary test runs don't count.

## Standing Rules (Active)

**L1 — Keep it small.** One module ideally. Small packages OK if they save time. Network access OK for fetching sample data.

**L2 — No JSON.** Fixtures and logs are fixed-width plain-text, one line per record, columns aligned for eye-scanning. JSON was explicitly rejected as too verbose.

**L3 — Auto-repair log damage.** Corrupt or torn depot-log lines are repaired and compacted automatically on next run. Keeping corrupt bytes around was rejected.

**L4 — Testing focused on happy path.** Feature breadth is the priority for the demo. Restart/failure testing waits until after the pitch. Smoke tests of the happy path are in-scope.

**L6 — No refactoring module layout.** Current file structure stays as-is. No splitting into packages, no moving functions between files. (Packaging a copy for a friend to try is fine as a simple archive whenever asked.)

---

The summary describes work that contradicts L2, L3, and L6 (JSON-lines logging, corruption detection instead of auto-repair, refactored package structure, crash recovery tests). That work is either stale or needs your confirmation to supersede those constraints.
